function: BS precoding for weighted sum-rate maximization in multicell-cooperation MU-MIMO downlink: unfolded distributed WMMSE learns step sizes and power factors that set the precoders (pp. 1, 6).
system: B=3 cells, Nt=4 or 8 BS antennas, Nr=1 or 2 per user, Kb=2 users per cell, per-BS power limit; no RIS; band not stated (pp. 2, 9, 11).
method: Deep-unfolded distributed WMMSE (USD-WMMSE, USD-WMMSE-TLM) with trainable step sizes and power factors; unsupervised training on a negative weighted sum-rate loss, mini-batch Adam (pp. 1, 7, 9).
data_channel: Own simulator: Rayleigh fading with 30+25log10(d) dB path loss, BS distance 500 m, users dropped in 500 m circles; 150,000 training and 1,000 test samples (p. 8).
test_conditions: Same Rayleigh model for training and testing; trained at 46 dBm, tested at 46, 36, 26 dBm; trained with T=12 layers, tested with T=3, 6, 12 (p. 10).
baselines: Non-learned: centralized WMMSE, synchronous and asynchronous distributed WMMSE, SD-WMMSE-MLM; learned: centralized IAIDNN [28], an earlier deep-unfolding precoder (pp. 8-9, 15).
metrics: Average sum rate (bps/Hz), FLOPs, CSI exchange overhead, and information exchange time (pp. 8-12).
complexity: Distributed O(B^2) versus centralized O(B^3) in the number of BSs; FLOPs in Table V, e.g., USD-WMMSE 44,640 versus C-WMMSE 97,632 at (3,4,1,2), L=3, T=3 (pp. 1, 11).
openness: none; 'our open source Marveltoolbox' is cited through a journal reference [40] without link, and no code or data of the method is released (p. 9).
q1_support: p. 8: "a Rayleigh fading channel model" with own path loss 30 + 25log10(d) dB; no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO, or measured data is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 10: "trained with different transmit power in Table III"; this changes the transmit power (SNR) and, in Table IV, the number of layers T, with the same channel model, antennas, and users, so it is read as an SNR sweep and not a new scenario.
q3_support: p. 9: "Centralized IAIDNN [28]" is the earlier learned deep-unfolding precoder; non-learned baselines are C-WMMSE, SD-WMMSE, and AD-WMMSE; Fig. 4 (p. 8) plots the sum rate of all of them.
q4_support: p. 8: "The computational complexity of each method is listed" in Table I (FLOPs per step); Table V (p. 11) gives FLOPs of every method, e.g., 44,640 for USD-WMMSE versus 97,632 for C-WMMSE at (3,4,1,2).
q5_support: p. 9: "our open source Marveltoolbox in [40]"; [40] is a journal reference with no link or DOI for this method, the data are simulated, and no release of the USD-WMMSE code is stated.
notes: First page title matches the DOI. Tables I-VIII and Figs. 4-8 are images, read from pp. 8, 9, 11, 12. q2 and q5 are borderline: the authors call the transmit-power and layer-count tests generalization and mention an open-source toolbox. I read the first as an SNR sweep and depth truncation, and the second as no release with a link.
